newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge sends tax protest group leader to jail.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge sends tax protest group leader to jail.

text.p: A federal judge in Texas Thursday sentenced the leader of a tax protest organization to 97 months in prison for his role in a $61 million bogus money order scheme, the Justice Department said.
It said Gerald Henson, 56, who was convicted last June on fraud and conspiracy charges, also received a $10,000 fine as part of the sentence handed down by U.S. District Judge James Nowlin in Austin.
Henson sponsored seminars promoting the use of bogus money orders and other anti-tax ideas, department officials said.

Under the scheme, Henson sold promotional packages containing six blank bogus money orders for $300. Buyers filled out the orders for any amount they wanted, and then used them to pay the Internal Revenue Service, credit card companies, mortgage lenders and others, the officials said.

Henson owned a commercial printing company in Oklahoma. Besides printing the money orders, he also printed and sold numerous tax protest publications denouncing the authority of the IRS and the federal government, the officials said.
